method.description: Attempted official download of three Missouri documents, refusal classified with the hardened acquisition-response validator rather than by reading the status code, and the resulting disposition recorded per identity against what the repository already holds.
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires preserving the 403/WAF disposition distinctly, recording attended-retrieval evidence only, and never relabelling the source as generically missing or inferring an alternative. The block is characterised to its vendor and signal. No source is relabelled missing. No alternative is inferred — in particular the circuit-court mirror the queue records for GN10 is expressly rejected rather than used.

evidence.bodyIsIssuerBrandedDetail: The refusal page is styled by the Missouri Courts themselves — it loads https://www.courts.mo.gov/mod/img/header.png as a banner — while being served through Cloudflare with a challenge-platform signal. It is an origin-branded error page in front of a Cloudflare mitigation, not the stock Cloudflare interstitial.

distinctFromSiblingBlocks.versusMinnesota: Minnesota is also Cloudflare and also 403, but it serves the stock 'Just a moment...' interstitial and returns cf-mitigated: challenge. Missouri returns an issuer-branded Error 403 page with a challenge-platform signal and no cf-mitigated header. Same vendor, different configuration and different body.
distinctFromSiblingBlocks.versusDelaware: Delaware is an F5 BIG-IP ASM policy returning HTTP 200 with a 'Request Rejected' body. Missouri returns an honest 403. The Delaware case is the one where status alone misleads.
distinctFromSiblingBlocks.versusMontana: Montana's courts.mt.gov accepts no connection at all. Missouri answers, and answers with a refusal.
distinctFromSiblingBlocks.whyThisMatters: Four blocked jurisdictions, four distinct signatures. A single automation-blocked label across them would lose the fact that only one is evadable-looking, only one is a true outage, and each needs a different remedy.

blockCharacterisation.notAMissingSource: The Missouri Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes all three documents and its forms index lists them. Nothing is missing.
blockCharacterisation.remedy: An attended human-in-browser session. That is the only legitimate route and none was attempted.
whatWasNotDone: No attempt to solve, replay or bypass the Cloudflare challenge.

No alternative document inferred for any of the three.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: all three documents, titles, roles and issuer are established and retained. It is not source_missing, which the stop condition forbids and which would be false. It is not acquired: the validator returns acquired=false with a null digest. And it is not a bare currentness hold, because for two identities there is affirmative evidence pointing at a reissue.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Missouri's refusal is recorded as a Cloudflare challenge-platform mitigation at HTTP 403 behind an issuer-branded error page, classified by the hardened validator rather than by status code, with acquired=false and a null digest. It is distinguished from the three other blocked jurisdictions in this programme, which use three different mechanisms and need three different remedies. A concrete supersession suspicion is recorded for CR300 and CR301 — a 01/01/25 index date against retained 2010 and 2017 stamps — turning a vague currentness hold into a specific question an attended session can answer in one visit. The one reachable GN10 mirror is expressly rejected with reasons. No binary is acquired, no receipt is created, nothing enters version control, no alternative is inferred, no source is relabelled missing, no component is rebound, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
